svg.title: MacSync kill chain - fake Toria wallet, iCloud calendar payload host and Finder-disguised backdoor on macOS
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the macOS victim: 1 a fake Toria crypto wallet promoted on X and Telegram, 2 a stage 1 app loader that clears the quarantine attribute and XOR-decrypts a URL from its overlay, 3 a stage 2 downloader that reads a public iCloud calendar and pipes its lines into zsh, 4 stage 3 and 4 droppers that decrypt a Mach-O into a hidden tmp file and check for virtual machines and debuggers, 5 stage 5 and 6 scripts that exchange keys with the C2, run the next stage in memory and install persistence, 6 an infostealer with a fake admin password prompt that collects Keychain, browser, wallet and developer data, 7 a backdoor disguised as Finder with a LaunchAgent, zshrc and git hook persistence. Right lane, the operator and infrastructure: A the malware-as-a-service operator, B the lure and installer domains, C Apple iCloud used as a payload host, D the C2 servers and backdoor protocol, E the chunked exfiltration, F the backdoor commands. Critical stages are shown in red.
svg.text: MacSync: iCloud calendar payload host and Finder-disguised backdoor
Vendor: Kaspersky Securelist - Date: 2026-09-24 - Cluster: MacSync MaaS (unattributed) - Day 114
TARGET: macOS USER (developer, crypto user)
OPERATOR AND INFRASTRUCTURE (what is known)
Fake Toria wallet lure on X and Telegram
Nonexistent crypto wallet app with its own web page, promoted
on X and Telegram; the chain starts with a malicious DMG image
Kaspersky: targets developers and crypto users on macOS
T1204.002 User Execution: Malicious File
toria[.]app warpcast[.]asia/Toria.dmg
Stage 1 loader clears quarantine, decrypts a URL
xattr -cr on its own bundle when com.apple.quarantine is set
XOR-decrypts a URL stored in the overlay, read back from SONOMAC1
XOR key is ASCII sonomabld plus 0x07; six loader hashes published
SONOMAC1 73 6f 6e 6f 6d 61 62 6c 64 07
Stage 2: downloader reads an iCloud calendar
Fetches installer.sh or a public iCloud calendar (.ics)
Pipes calendar lines into zsh -s; lines before DESCRIPTION: fail
Commands after it fetch Loader.app.tar.gz, strip quarantine, sign
caldav.icloud.com/published/ gateway.icloud.com/caldav/
Stages 3-4: droppers decrypt and hide a Mach-O
AES-CBC decrypts a zlib Mach-O to /tmp/.sys-<16 characters>
VM check: sysctl kern.hv_vmm_present, machdep.cpu.brand_string
ptrace PT_DENY_ATTACH blocks debuggers; AES-CBC shell script next
Sigma 03: TargetFilename matches /tmp/.sys-<16>
Stages 5-6: key exchange, memory stage, persistence
Curve25519 ECDH with the C2 (crypto v2.5), AES-GCM key unwrap
Runs the encrypted stage in memory (daemon_function)
Downloads stealer and backdoor, sets persistence, cleans /tmp
pkgunpack genkey / decrypt sn-dek-wrap-v1
Infostealer: fake password prompt, wide collection
Swift app asks for the admin password and verifies it via PAM
Collects Keychain, browsers, wallets, Telegram, SSH, AWS, K8s, git
Then shows a fake corrupted-application dialog
Uploads over PUT in 90 MB chunks (T1030)
Finder-disguised backdoor, many persistence points
LaunchAgent com.apple.finder.agent, .zshrc, global git hooks
Install dir ~/Library/Application Support/System; .repair-run
Kills BTMNotificationAgent and two other notification agents
Sigma 04 artifacts, Sigma 05 process kills
A
Operator: MaaS family, no attribution
Sold as malware-as-a-service; Mac.c in 2025, later MacSync
Early versions were AppleScript-based and AMOS-like
Kaspersky names no actor, victims or counts
New version spotted in September 2026
confidence: high (family), none for operator
Securelist 2026-09-24; Kaspersky release 2026-09-17
B
Lure and installer infrastructure
toria[.]app and warpcast[.]asia/Toria.dmg
installer.sh on streamyard. and waaako.appstore.com[.]mx
installer.sh on slack.apple03cloudstore[.]com
Look-alike names of Apple store and cloud services
Suricata 6310001-6310006 (DNS and SNI)
C
Apple infrastructure as payload host
Public iCloud calendar entry: commands in the DESCRIPTION: field
Calendar attachment holds Loader.app.tar.gz (gateway.icloud.com)
Legitimate Apple hosts: block the exact URL, never the domain
Detect the requesting process, not the destination
Sigma 01 and KQL k2: non-calendar process fetches one
D
C2 servers and backdoor protocol
docsend.appstore.com[.]mx and toria.apple03cloudstore[.]com
GET /v1/agent/ping returns cmd; POST /v1/agent/refresh renews token
POST /v1/asset/<id>/init, PUT /v1/asset/<id> with X-Upload-Token
HTTP with JSON responses
Suricata 6310007-8 and YARA rule 2
E
Exfiltration and scale
Stolen data staged in a hidden directory under /tmp
PUT requests in 90 MB chunks (earlier builds used other sizes)
File size and SHA-256 sent in X-File-Size and X-File-Sha256
No victim counts or geography published
Hunt H3: large PUT bodies, look-alike domain lookups
F
Backdoor commands
deploy_ext deploys a browser extension; deploy_ledger swaps Ledger
regrab recollects data into /tmp/osalogging.zip by default
live_browser loads sn_relay; its function is undocumented
Other commands run base64 AppleScript from script_b64
YARA rule 3: command names, key-derivation fields
Detection anchors: SONOMAC1 overlay, /tmp/.sys-*, com.apple.finder.agent, iCloud calendar fetch, 21 MD5s
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-05, KQL k1-k3, YARA macsync_sonomac_backdoor.yar (3 rules), Suricata sids 6310001-6310009, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
Hashes are MD5 only (21 published); domains rotate, so lean on staging paths, the Finder-disguised LaunchAgent and the calendar fetch.
iCloud hosts are legitimate Apple services: block exact URLs only. No sample was available; rules use Securelist-published strings.
